title_original: Galerie Écho 119 : Kusukazu Uraguchi : “à marée basse”

blocks.text: From 30 October 30, Galerie Écho 119 in Paris presents “à marée basse” (at low tide) , a new exhibition conceived with and by the curator Sonia Voss .

This journey into the depths of the ocean will be explored through the lens of photographer Kusukazu Uraguchi (1922–1988), who spent nearly thirty years photographing the ama (the Japanese women who free-drive) of his region, and French ceramicist Laure Gilquin (b. 1981), whose work draws inspiration from the forms and materials of the underwater world.

For over three thousand years, the ama – Japan’s ‘women of the sea’ – have inhabited the archipelago’s shores, free-diving in search of seaweed and abalone. Their sensual connection to the water, their fearlessness and their self-assurance have, over the centuries, fascinated poets and artists.

The Japanese photographer Kusukazu Uraguchi (1922–1988), originally from Shima (Mie Prefecture), devoted more than thirty years capturing the lives of the ama in his region. His photographs shed light on their age-old practices which were already under threat of disappearing at the time whilst capturing their energy in every moment. The exhibition draws on Uraguchi’s archive, which contains tens of thousands of negatives and had long remained unexplored.

Kusukazu Uraguchi was born in 1922 in Fuseda, Shima. After the war, he worked as a pearl merchant before turning his hand to photography; his early career was marked by the publication of a photograph in Camera Mainichi in 1956. From 1972 onwards, his photographs appeared regularly in several Japanese magazines and were exhibited throughout Japan. He published Shima Fudoki in 1978, followed by Shima no ama in 1982, both books devoted to his native region. He died of pneumonia in 1988.
His work was brought back to the public’s attention at the Rencontres d’Arles 2024 thanks to the efforts of curator Sonia Voss.

The exhibition will be followed by a presentation at Paris Photo (12–15 November) featuring a display on the theme of ‘female divers’, again showcasing the work of Kusukazu Uraguchi , alongside that of artist-researcher Laure Winants and Japanese photographer Kazuo Kitai .
